redirects.//: The testing address is retired. Anything still pointing at it — an old bookmark, a link somewhere, a crawler that saw it once — lands on the real domain instead, on the same path. A permanent redirect rather than a noindex header: this makes the duplicate stop existing rather than merely asking search engines to look away, and it hands whatever the old address had earned to the domain.

headers.//: Every preview build Vercel makes is another copy of the site on its own address. None of them should ever be indexed.
The verification file must be served as plain text, exactly as Google wrote it.
The pages behind the connection place real trades. A stale one served from a cache would be an old build talking to Deriv, so they are re-fetched every time; the assets around them are safe to keep.
Ordinary hardening. Nothing here frames another site or is meant to be framed.
